newsitem.title: USA: Killing frost ends Minnesota's growing season.
newsitem.headline: Killing frost ends Minnesota's growing season.

text.p: A killing frost covered Minnesota Wednesday night and Thursday morning last week which ended the row crop growing season, according to the Minnesota Agricultural Statistics Service.
The frost was welcomed by many soybean growers whose fields had reached maturity. Weeds were also killed by the freeze and plant stems were made easier to combine.

Soybean harvest stood at 20 percent complete as of Sunday, up from three percent a week ago and ahead of 16 percent a year ago but behind the 27 percent average. Eighty-four percent of the crop was mature, up from 37 percent a week ago.
Six percent of the corn crop was harvested, up from three percent a week ago, but behind 16 percent a year ago and 11 percent average.
Eighty-seven percent of the corn crop was mature, up from 43 percent a week ago, behind 99 percent a year ago but ahead of the 71 percent five-year average.
Topsoil moisture was seven percent very short, 27 percent short, 61 percent adequate and five percent surplus.
